| On the live view, the monitor reads BC Wildfire Service fire points and perimeters from this site's mirror, joined by fire number. The visible live view checks the mirror every fifteen minutes. If the mirror is unavailable on entry, the monitor tries the newest captured fleet day and labels it as a dated sample. Statuses of Out are excluded. Satellite hotspots are NRCan CWFIS last-24-h detections, used only on the live view when its mirror answers. On the live view, available Open-Meteo 850 hPa winds affect transit times and target scoring. The mirror limits wind requests to once an hour. The monitor interpolates its coarse BC grid to route midpoints. Missing or stale wind means still air. Weather data by [link] (CC BY 4.0). Where the BC record supplies an official incident link, the monitor provides it. Exercise fires have no official incident page. Data, licences and notices records the sources and their terms. For a real emergency use the BC Wildfire Service, not this page. Source selection is a size-weighted choice among definite water bodies meeting the class's area and distance rules, larger water preferred over just-qualifying. Fleet allocation scores eligible fires by size, class fit and source distance. Also computed are routes, phase durations, pump and drag and descent power, nitrogen mass-energy cycling, and throughput. The arithmetic section explains selected formulas. | Rods only win where buckling stops governing — below about six diameters of length — and every member here is thirty to sixty diameters long. (The one place rods do belong is the floater's level-2 boom chords at ~1.7 mm, where no tube can be made.) Round beats a hexagonal section by 9.4% on Euler at identical mass, and by far more on the flight article, where the wall is thin enough that local buckling co-governs and a flat face has no curvature to stabilise it; hex would buy anti-rotation and a flat bonding land, and we need neither. | six | The occurrence needs a ledger entry or a rewording. floatcheck floatcheck | ledger entry or rewording |

| A later run recomputes all of it and fails naming any member-end whose properties moved, which is what makes optimising these joints for weight safe to start: shrink a node and quietly take engagement with it, and the build goes red with the arms named. 12 of the 16 proofs pass, and they are the ones assembly turns on — every one of the 332 closing ends carries a pilot inside its own swing-in bound and none is at the full stub, and the swing is now swept end by end rather than sampled; the seat is a real land of 28.274 mm² — the whole pipe annulus, at every one of the 432 ends now that no mating plane cuts a socket — rather than the blend fillet the pipe used to come down on; the crush ribs survive the slot that used to delete them; no slot starts closer than the declared 0.500 mm to the feature it would foul; every pipe's own annulus is empty for its whole travel; and every member-end is priced at a load derived from the path that puts it there rather than at one number wearing 432 hats. | 12 | The occurrence needs a ledger entry or a rewording. floatcheck floatcheck | ledger entry or rewording |
